summary: A group call-review session run by Chris Klevan, who appears to be the sales manager - he states 'that's why I hired you' to Andrew Musial. The team plays back and critiques a discovery call Andrew ran with a prospect referred to as Hugh, with Ben Byrne and Kyla Louie contributing. Coaching centres on three themes: holding emotional space instead of moving to the next question, replacing leading and binary questions with open-ended ones, and using silence to make prospects keep talking. Chris also sets out his position on qualifying for money on a fitness offer, and explains that stacking emotional anchors through discovery is what stops a prospect scoffing when the 6K price lands. The recording ends mid-sentence while Kyla is asking a process question about rescheduling another rep's lead.
notable: The prospect under review discloses EDS (Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, a connective-tissue disorder), a prior elbow surgery, a kneecap that feels like it is dislocating, hip flexor weakness, lower back pain, ADD, and that he is under both a chiropractor and a physical therapist. Nobody on the call raises medical clearance at any point; he is discussed purely as a closeable opportunity.

Chris Klevan states the qualifying policy for fitness offers: 'I don't really care about their finances unless they tell me straight up I genuinely can't afford anything', and 'if it's a big enough problem, they'll find the money, usually'.

Chris describes redirecting a prospect's emergency credit toward the purchase: 'maybe they think they don't have a lot of money, but they have a $20,000 credit card sitting there that they're like, only for emergencies. And it's like, well, you think this is an emergency?'
The reviewed prospect had already disclosed constrained finances affecting his food: 'At the moment, money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, because it's cheaper.'

Chris names fallback paths outside the two-tier offer: 'we'll work on a plan, or I'll get them in the primal university for a bit, or something. I'll find a way to make it work. Or maybe we finance them'.

Chris explains the mechanism behind anchoring: 'they'll keep reestablishing that anchor inside of them, so it's all going to come up at the end of the close once they hear the price drop. They're going to have so many anchors of emotional moments... that they're not going to scoff at 6K.'
Andrew Musial uses the word 'retard' to describe a questioning style; Ben Byrne pushes back ('I don't know if retard is...') and Chris reframes it as 'childlike curiosity'.
Chris and Ben cite prior experience on Cole Gordon's sales teams as the benchmark for the standard being coached.

Chris coaches diagnostic neutrality and warns against validating language mid-discovery: 'Be careful using any language in a discovery call that's like, oh, that's good, okay, yeah, you're doing well. I treat it like a doctor... Like a diagnosis'.
Ben Byrne leaves the meeting early at 00:36:22 to take the Tristan Chalmers call recorded the same day: 'I got Tristan guys in my room'.
Kyla Louie's closing question - whether she may reschedule another rep's lead without speaking to them - is cut off by the end of the recording, so the answer and any policy on it are not captured.
